title: Hujin Harbor in Yangyang: A Beginner's Guide to Korea's Quiet East-Coast Fishing Village
html:
If you're exploring Korea's east coast and want to see a real, working fishing village instead of just a resort beach, Hujin Harbor (후진항, "Hujinhang") in Yangyang County, Gangwon-do, is an easy and charming stop. It's small — you can see the whole place in 20–30 minutes — but it has a red lighthouse, anchored fishing boats, fresh seafood stalls, and a lively weekend market. This guide covers what's there, how to get there without a car, and what else is nearby if you want to make a day of it.

What Is Hujin Harbor Like?

Hujin Harbor is a small, working fishing port on Korea's East Sea coast. Unlike a big tourist beach, this is where local fishing boats actually come in with their catch. The port is marked by a photogenic red lighthouse at the end of the breakwater, with small boats bobbing in the water and a row of simple seafood stalls ("hwe centers," 회센터) selling the day's catch — mostly raw fish (hoe) and shellfish you can eat on the spot. It's free to walk around, open all day, and parking is available right next to the harbor.

How to Get to Hujin Harbor From Seoul

Hujin Harbor is in Yangyang County, which is about 2 to 2.5 hours from Seoul, so it works best as part of a longer east-coast trip rather than a quick half-day visit.

  • Express bus (simplest): Take an intercity/express bus from Seoul Express Bus Terminal to Yangyang Bus Terminal (roughly 2 hours, buses run frequently throughout the day). From Yangyang Bus Terminal, Hujin Harbor is a short local taxi ride (around 10–15 minutes).
  • Train + bus: There's no train station in Yangyang itself, so you'd take a train to Gangneung Station first, then transfer to a local bus or taxi north to Yangyang. This takes longer overall than the direct express bus, so it only makes sense if you're coming through Gangneung anyway.
  • Rental car: If you're already driving the east coast, Hujin Harbor sits just off the coastal road and has its own parking area, so it's an easy stop to add between other sights.

The Hujin Beach Market (Weekends Only)

On select weekends, Hujin Harbor hosts the Hujin Beach Market, a small outdoor flea market right along the water with local food stalls, handmade goods, and sometimes live music. It's a nice chance to see a laid-back, local side of a Korean coastal town rather than a touristy shopping street.

⚠️ The exact schedule has been reported differently by different sources — some say it runs on the second weekend of each month, others say the second and fourth weekends. Typical hours are roughly 10 AM to 6–7 PM. Since outdoor markets like this can change or pause with the seasons, it's worth searching "후진항 비치마켓" (Hujin Beach Market) or checking a Korean map app for the latest dates right before your trip, rather than planning your whole visit around it.

What Else Is Nearby, and Practical Tips

Hujin Harbor sits in a part of Yangyang that's popular with Korean surfers and beachgoers, so there's plenty to pair it with:

  • Seorak Beach (설악해수욕장): A clean, shallow beach popular for surfing, about a 5-minute walk from the harbor.
  • Naksansa Temple (낙산사): A cliffside Buddhist temple nearby, famous for its ocean-view terrace and large standing statue of the Goddess of Mercy — a great add-on if you enjoy temples with a view.
  • Seafood right at the harbor: The hwe centers at Hujin sell fresh raw fish and shellfish by weight. If you've never ordered hoe (raw fish) before, staff are used to helping first-timers pick something mild — just point and ask, and know that prices can vary by season and catch.

A few more tips for a smooth visit:

  • There's no entry fee for the harbor itself — you only pay if you buy food, market goods, or activities.
  • Weekends (especially during the market) get busy with local visitors, so arrive earlier in the day if you want a quieter look around.
  • This is a small, low-English-signage fishing village, not a major tourist attraction — it's best suited to travelers who enjoy a quieter, more local-feeling stop rather than those looking for big attractions or English-friendly service.

meta_description: A beginner's guide to Hujin Harbor, Yangyang: a quiet fishing port with a red lighthouse, weekend market, seafood stalls, and how to get there.
